summary: 1934 CCC-built 60-foot Aermotor-type fire tower on Carson Springs Road, Cocke County, Tennessee; NHLR-registered 2014 and NRHP-nominated 2015. Current access and staffing not documented.

facts.design: 60-foot steel truss tower with seven-by-seven-foot cab; likely Aermotor MC-39 type; Carnegie Steel marker
facts.status_note: NRHP nomination lists current functions as emergency fire lookout and vacant, not in use; not used for observation since the mid-1970s; surveyed in overall good condition

access.note: NRHP survey found the observation room trapdoor locked and the cab interior inaccessible. No current visit rules found; Wikipedia says the only access is Carson Springs Road.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 3,617 ft (1,102 m) and the NRHP nomination gives 3,629 feet. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination is the strongest source and covers build, design, deed and condition, but it has little on this tower's history (it says so directly). No staffing names or specific fires were found. The nomination dates the cabin replacement to 1960 (removed sometime after 1985) and says the tower was used for fire detection and constantly manned until the 1970s; the story reports the cabin and current-use facts from it. The 'staffed' event is an inference from the operator's cabin. Access is recorded as restricted only because the trapdoor was locked at survey; no current visit information was found. The Wikipedia access line attributes the single access to NPS; the NPS page itself was not read. Elevation conflict: NHLR 3,617 ft vs nomination 3,629 ft. Registry number conflict: the nomination gives US 993, TN 13, while NHLR gives US 993, TN 14 (the JSON uses NHLR; the story does not mention it). The 2015 NRHP date is the NPGallery 'Date Published' value; the exact listing date was not confirmed. The brief's height 18.3 m matches the nomination's sixty feet. The NHLR page fetched did not include a description. Verification 2026-10-08: the story's cabin sentence now gives the 1960 replacement and its later removal, and the current-use sentence now lists both the emergency-lookout and not-in-use functions.
